units.leftText: Simon Peter, a servant and apostle of Jesus Christ, To those who through the righteousness of our God and Savior Jesus Christ have received a faith as precious as ours:
units.rightText: Simon Peter, a servant and apostle of Jesus Christ, to them that have obtained a like precious faith with us in the righteousness of our God and the Saviour Jesus Christ:

units.leftText: Grace and peace be multiplied to you through the knowledge of God and of Jesus our Lord. Partakers of the Divine Nature
units.rightText: Grace to you and peace be multiplied in the knowledge of God and of Jesus our Lord;

units.leftText: His divine power has given us everything we need for life and godliness through the knowledge of Him who called us by His own glory and excellence.
units.rightText: seeing that his divine power hath granted unto us all things that pertain unto life and godliness, through the knowledge of him that called us by his own glory and virtue;

units.leftText: Through these He has given us His precious and magnificent promises, so that through them you may become partakers of the divine nature, now that you have escaped the corruption in the world caused by evil desires.
units.rightText: whereby he hath granted unto us his precious and exceeding great promises; that through these ye may become partakers of the divine nature, having escaped from the corruption that is in the world by lust.

units.leftText: For this very reason, make every effort to add to your faith virtue; and to virtue, knowledge;
units.rightText: Yea, and for this very cause adding on your part all diligence, in your faith supply virtue; and in your virtue knowledge;

units.leftText: and to knowledge, self-control; and to self-control, perseverance; and to perseverance, godliness;
units.rightText: and in your knowledge self-control; and in your self-control patience; and in your patience godliness;

units.leftText: and to godliness, brotherly kindness; and to brotherly kindness, love.
units.rightText: and in your godliness brotherly kindness; and in your brotherly kindness love.

units.leftText: For if you possess these qualities and continue to grow in them, they will keep you from being ineffective and unproductive in your knowledge of our Lord Jesus Christ.
units.rightText: For if these things are yours and abound, they make you to be not idle nor unfruitful unto the knowledge of our Lord Jesus Christ.

units.leftText: But whoever lacks these traits is nearsighted to the point of blindness, having forgotten that he has been cleansed from his past sins.
units.rightText: For he that lacketh these things is blind, seeing only what is near, having forgotten the cleansing from his old sins.

units.leftText: Therefore, brothers, strive to make your calling and election sure. For if you practice these things you will never stumble,
units.rightText: Wherefore, brethren, give the more diligence to make your calling and election sure: for if ye do these things, ye shall never stumble:

units.leftText: and you will receive a lavish reception into the eternal kingdom of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ.
units.rightText: for thus shall be richly supplied unto you the entrance into the eternal kingdom of our Lord and Saviour Jesus Christ.

units.leftText: Therefore I will always remind you of these things, even though you know them and are established in the truth you now have.
units.rightText: Wherefore I shall be ready always to put you in remembrance of these things, though ye know them, and are established in the truth which is with you.

units.leftText: I think it is right to refresh your memory as long as I live in the tent of my body,
units.rightText: And I think it right, as long as I am in this tabernacle, to stir you up by putting you in remembrance;
leftNotes: 1:13 Literally as long as I am in this tent

units.leftText: because I know that this tent will soon be laid aside, as our Lord Jesus Christ has made clear to me.
units.rightText: knowing that the putting off of my tabernacle cometh swiftly, even as our Lord Jesus Christ signified unto me.

units.leftText: And I will make every effort to ensure that after my departure, you will be able to recall these things at all times. Eyewitnesses of His Majesty (Matthew 17:1–13|MAT 17:1-13*; Mark 9:1–13|MRK 9:1-13*; Luke 9:28–36|LUK 9:28-36*)
units.rightText: Yea, I will give diligence that at every time ye may be able after my decease to call these things to remembrance.

units.leftText: For we did not follow cleverly devised fables when we made known to you the power and coming of our Lord Jesus Christ, but we were eyewitnesses of His majesty.
units.rightText: For we did not follow cunningly devised fables, when we made known unto you the power and coming of our Lord Jesus Christ, but we were eyewitnesses of his majesty.

units.leftText: For He received honor and glory from God the Father when the voice came to Him from the Majestic Glory, saying, “This is My beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased.”
units.rightText: For he received from God the Father honor and glory, when there was borne such a voice to him by the Majestic Glory, This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased:
leftNotes: 1:17 Matthew 17:5|MAT 17:5*; see also Mark 9:7 and Luke 9:35.

units.leftText: And we ourselves heard this voice from heaven when we were with Him on the holy mountain.
units.rightText: and this voice we ourselves heard borne out of heaven, when we were with him in the holy mount.

units.leftText: We also have the word of the prophets as confirmed beyond doubt. And you will do well to pay attention to it, as to a lamp shining in a dark place, until the day dawns and the morning star rises in your hearts.
units.rightText: And we have the word of prophecy made more sure; whereunto ye do well that ye take heed, as unto a lamp shining in a dark place, until the day dawn, and the day-star arise in your hearts:

units.leftText: Above all, you must understand that no prophecy of Scripture comes from one’s own interpretation.
units.rightText: knowing this first, that no prophecy of scripture is of private interpretation.

units.leftText: For no such prophecy was ever brought forth by the will of man, but men spoke from God as they were carried along by the Holy Spirit.
units.rightText: For no prophecy ever came by the will of man: but men spake from God, being moved by the Holy Spirit.

units.leftText: Now there were also false prophets among the people, just as there will be false teachers among you. They will secretly introduce destructive heresies, even denying the Master who bought them — bringing swift destruction on themselves.
units.rightText: But there arose false prophets also among the people, as among you also there shall be false teachers, who shall privily bring in destructive heresies, denying even the Master that bought them, bringing upon themselves swift destruction.

units.leftText: Many will follow in their depravity, and because of them the way of truth will be defamed.
units.rightText: And many shall follow their lascivious doings; by reason of whom the way of the truth shall be evil spoken of.

units.leftText: In their greed, these false teachers will exploit you with deceptive words. The longstanding verdict against them remains in force, and their destruction does not sleep.
units.rightText: And in covetousness shall they with feigned words make merchandise of you: whose sentence now from of old lingereth not, and their destruction slumbereth not.

units.leftText: For if God did not spare the angels when they sinned, but cast them deep into hell, placing them in chains of darkness to be held for judgment;
units.rightText: For if God spared not angels when they sinned, but cast them down to hell, and committed them to pits of darkness, to be reserved unto judgment;
leftNotes: 2:4 Greek cast them into Tartarus; see the First Book of Enoch (1 Enoch 13:1–11|13:1-11* and 1 Enoch 20:1–4).

units.leftText: if He did not spare the ancient world when He brought the flood on its ungodly people, but preserved Noah, a preacher of righteousness, among the eight;
units.rightText: and spared not the ancient world, but preserved Noah with seven others, a preacher of righteousness, when he brought a flood upon the world of the ungodly;

units.leftText: if He condemned the cities of Sodom and Gomorrah to destruction, reducing them to ashes as an example of what is coming on the ungodly;
units.rightText: and turning the cities of Sodom and Gomorrah into ashes condemned them with an overthrow, having made them an example unto those that should live ungodly;
leftNotes: 2:6 WH does not include to destruction.
2:6 Or on future generations of the ungodly

units.leftText: and if He rescued Lot, a righteous man distressed by the depraved conduct of the lawless
units.rightText: and delivered righteous Lot, sore distressed by the lascivious life of the wicked

units.leftText: (for that righteous man, living among them day after day, was tormented in his righteous soul by the lawless deeds he saw and heard )—
units.rightText: (for that righteous man dwelling among them, in seeing and hearing, vexed his righteous soul from day to day with their lawless deeds):

units.leftText: if all this is so, then the Lord knows how to rescue the godly from trials and to hold the unrighteous for punishment on the day of judgment.
units.rightText: the Lord knoweth how to deliver the godly out of temptation, and to keep the unrighteous under punishment unto the day of judgment;

units.leftText: Such punishment is specially reserved for those who indulge the corrupt desires of the flesh and despise authority. Bold and self-willed, they are unafraid to slander glorious beings.
units.rightText: but chiefly them that walk after the flesh in the lust of defilement, and despise dominion. Daring, self-willed, they tremble not to rail at dignities:

units.leftText: Yet not even angels, though greater in strength and power, dare to bring such slanderous charges against them before the Lord.
units.rightText: whereas angels, though greater in might and power, bring not a railing judgment against them before the Lord.

units.leftText: These men are like irrational animals, creatures of instinct, born to be captured and destroyed. They blaspheme in matters they do not understand, and like such creatures, they too will be destroyed.
units.rightText: But these, as creatures without reason, born mere animals to be taken and destroyed, railing in matters whereof they are ignorant, shall in their destroying surely be destroyed,

units.leftText: The harm they will suffer is the wages of their wickedness.
units.rightText: suffering wrong as the hire of wrong-doing; men that count it pleasure to revel in the day-time, spots and blemishes, revelling in their deceivings while they feast with you;

units.leftText: Their eyes are full of adultery; their desire for sin is never satisfied; they seduce the unstable. They are accursed children with hearts trained in greed.
units.rightText: having eyes full of adultery, and that cannot cease from sin; enticing unstedfast souls; having a heart exercised in covetousness; children of cursing;

units.leftText: They have left the straight way and wandered off to follow the way of Balaam son of Beor, who loved the wages of wickedness.
units.rightText: forsaking the right way, they went astray, having followed the way of Balaam the son of Beor, who loved the hire of wrong-doing;
leftNotes: 2:15 NA, SBL, BYZ, and TR Bosor

units.leftText: But he was rebuked for his transgression by a donkey, otherwise without speech, that spoke with a man’s voice and restrained the prophet’s madness.
units.rightText: but he was rebuked for his own transgression: a dumb ass spake with man’s voice and stayed the madness of the prophet.

units.leftText: These men are springs without water and mists driven by a storm. Blackest darkness is reserved for them.
units.rightText: These are springs without water, and mists driven by a storm; for whom the blackness of darkness hath been reserved.

units.leftText: With lofty but empty words, they appeal to the sensual passions of the flesh and entice those who are just escaping from others who live in error.
units.rightText: For, uttering great swelling words of vanity, they entice in the lusts of the flesh, by lasciviousness, those who are just escaping from them that live in error;

units.leftText: They promise them freedom, while they themselves are slaves to depravity. For a man is a slave to whatever has mastered him.
units.rightText: promising them liberty, while they themselves are bondservants of corruption; for of whom a man is overcome, of the same is he also brought into bondage.

units.leftText: If indeed they have escaped the corruption of the world through the knowledge of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ, only to be entangled and overcome by it again, their final condition is worse than it was at first.
units.rightText: For if, after they have escaped the defilements of the world through the knowledge of the Lord and Saviour Jesus Christ, they are again entangled therein and overcome, the last state is become worse with them than the first.
leftNotes: 2:20 SBL and WH the Lord and Savior Jesus Christ

units.leftText: It would have been better for them not to have known the way of righteousness than to have known it and then to turn away from the holy commandment passed on to them.
units.rightText: For it were better for them not to have known the way of righteousness, than, after knowing it, to turn back from the holy commandment delivered unto them.

units.leftText: Of them the proverbs are true: “A dog returns to its vomit,” and, “A sow that is washed goes back to her wallowing in the mud.”
units.rightText: It has happened unto them according to the true proverb, The dog turning to his own vomit again, and the sow that had washed to wallowing in the mire.

units.leftText: Beloved, this is now my second letter to you. Both of them are reminders to stir you to wholesome thinking
units.rightText: This is now, beloved, the second epistle that I write unto you; and in both of them I stir up your sincere mind by putting you in remembrance;

units.leftText: by recalling what was foretold by the holy prophets and commanded by our Lord and Savior through your apostles.
units.rightText: that ye should remember the words which were spoken before by the holy prophets, and the commandment of the Lord and Saviour through your apostles:

units.leftText: Most importantly, you must understand that in the last days scoffers will come, scoffing and following their own evil desires.
units.rightText: knowing this first, that in the last days mockers shall come with mockery, walking after their own lusts,

units.leftText: “Where is the promise of His coming?” they will ask. “Ever since our fathers fell asleep, everything continues as it has from the beginning of creation.”
units.rightText: and saying, Where is the promise of his coming? for, from the day that the fathers fell asleep, all things continue as they were from the beginning of the creation.

units.leftText: But they deliberately overlook the fact that long ago by God’s word the heavens existed and the earth was formed out of water and by water,
units.rightText: For this they wilfully forget, that there were heavens from of old, and an earth compacted out of water and amidst water, by the word of God;

units.leftText: through which the world of that time perished in the flood.
units.rightText: by which means the world that then was, being overflowed with water, perished:

units.leftText: And by that same word, the present heavens and earth are reserved for fire, being kept for the day of judgment and destruction of ungodly men. The Day of the Lord (Zephaniah 1:7–18|ZEP 1:7-18*; Malachi 4:1–6|MAL 4:1-6*; 1 Thessalonians 5:1–11|1TH 5:1-11*)
units.rightText: but the heavens that now are, and the earth, by the same word have been stored up for fire, being reserved against the day of judgment and destruction of ungodly men.

units.leftText: Beloved, do not let this one thing escape your notice: With the Lord a day is like a thousand years, and a thousand years are like a day.
units.rightText: But forget not this one thing, beloved, that one day is with the Lord as a thousand years, and a thousand years as one day.

units.leftText: The Lord is not slow in keeping His promise as some understand slowness, but is patient with you, not wanting anyone to perish but everyone to come to repentance.
units.rightText: The Lord is not slack concerning his promise, as some count slackness; but is longsuffering to you-ward, not wishing that any should perish, but that all should come to repentance.

units.leftText: But the Day of the Lord will come like a thief. The heavens will disappear with a roar, the elements will be destroyed by fire, and the earth and its works will be laid bare.
units.rightText: But the day of the Lord will come as a thief; in the which the heavens shall pass away with a great noise, and the elements shall be dissolved with fervent heat, and the earth and the works that are therein shall be burned up.
leftNotes: 3:10 Or dissolved; also in verses 11 and 12.
3:10 Or will not be found. BYZ and TR will be burned up; SBL, NE, and WH will be found, i.e., will be unable to hide.

units.leftText: Since everything will be destroyed in this way, what kind of people ought you to be? You ought to conduct yourselves in holiness and godliness
units.rightText: Seeing that these things are thus all to be dissolved, what manner of persons ought ye to be in all holy living and godliness,

units.leftText: as you anticipate and hasten the coming of the day of God, when the heavens will be destroyed by fire and the elements will melt in the heat.
units.rightText: looking for and earnestly desiring the coming of the day of God, by reason of which the heavens being on fire shall be dissolved, and the elements shall melt with fervent heat?

units.leftText: But in keeping with God’s promise, we are looking forward to a new heaven and a new earth, where righteousness dwells. Final Exhortations
units.rightText: But, according to his promise, we look for new heavens and a new earth, wherein dwelleth righteousness.

units.leftText: Therefore, beloved, as you anticipate these things, make every effort to be found at peace— spotless and blameless in His sight.
units.rightText: Wherefore, beloved, seeing that ye look for these things, give diligence that ye may be found in peace, without spot and blameless in his sight.
leftNotes: 3:14 Or to be found by Him in peace, without spot and without blemish.

units.leftText: Consider also that our Lord’s patience brings salvation, just as our beloved brother Paul also wrote you with the wisdom God gave him.
units.rightText: And account that the longsuffering of our Lord is salvation; even as our beloved brother Paul also, according to the wisdom given to him, wrote unto you;

units.leftText: He writes this way in all his letters, speaking in them about such matters. Some parts of his letters are hard to understand, which ignorant and unstable people distort, as they do the rest of the Scriptures, to their own destruction.
units.rightText: as also in all his epistles, speaking in them of these things; wherein are some things hard to be understood, which the ignorant and unstedfast wrest, as they do also the other scriptures, unto their own destruction.

units.leftText: Therefore, beloved, since you already know these things, be on your guard so that you will not be carried away by the error of the lawless and fall from your secure standing.
units.rightText: Ye therefore, beloved, knowing these things beforehand, beware lest, being carried away with the error of the wicked, ye fall from your own stedfastness.

units.leftText: But grow in the grace and knowledge of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ. To Him be the glory both now and to the day of eternity. Amen.
units.rightText: But grow in the grace and knowledge of our Lord and Saviour Jesus Christ. To him be the glory both now and for ever. Amen.
leftNotes: 3:18 NE, WH, and NA do not include Amen.
